segments.text: Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in office, first as the Chief Minister of Gujarat and then as the Prime Minister for almost the last 12 years.
On this occasion, we wanted to speak about Prime Minister Modi's politics and how he has driven the BJP into this election winning machine.
No better than to speak on this than Mr. Suhail Seth, who has seen the journey of politicians from the Congress rule to the BJP rule.
BJP rule also under Mr. Vajpayee, now Mr. Modi.
Mr. Suhail Seth, welcome to CNN News 18.
I wanted to ask you that, you know, do you think has Modi become a brand so powerful that BJP can sell almost any election around him?
Absolutely.
See, you have to understand that Narendra Modi is not a part-time politician.
He's a full-time politician.
He is rooted to the soil.
He travels, he meets different people.
If you know him as reasonably well as I do, he's amongst one of the finest listeners you will ever meet.
His capacity to listen, his capacity to absorb, and more importantly, his capacity to course correct is remarkable.
You saw that recently with the cockroach movement.
Narendra Modi has had three distinctive bents of mind to him from a brand perspective.
The clear benefit that you get from Narendra Modi, number one is, here is a politician who is driven by, of and from the people.

everything has done, whether it was the cleaning up of the Savarmathi, whether it was installing solar panels on top, whether it was cleaning up Ahmedabad, more importantly making Gujarat the hub of investment, it's been done by Narendra Modi.
Second, it's very difficult for someone who was Chief Minister to come as Prime Minister
and then bring to bear his stamp on that office, because from a state you're running an entire nation.
And he did that.
What did he do?
He adopted some of the things that the Congress had thought of, but couldn't implement, whether it was the Aadhaar for KYC, whether it was Manrega.
Narendra Modi understands one thing that the benefit of the people must have no creditors and must have no debtors.
It's not as if you have to credit him for everything.
Third, he's driven adroitly by only one thing and one thing alone, is how do I make this country more relevant?
I've said this on your channel multiple times.
If I were to look at brand Narendra Modi, and I've said this

The brand today is muscular, it is identified with India, it has been able to rekindle the spirit of hope and aspiration amongst the youth of this country, whether it was through unicorns made in India, made for India, made by India, startup India.
What is equally important is the thrust towards digitization.
Very little known fact is 4,40,000 crores was the leakage in the direct benefit transfers in 2014.
That was plugged.
Rajiv Gandhi had famously said that out of every one rupee, only 15 paisa reaches the intended beneficiary.
Modi understands technology.
He understands the use of technology because technology is a great negator of corruption.
Because when you have technology, you have inbuilt transparency and you have less subjectivity.
You know, you can't be subjective.
So I think Modi will be remembered for
three or four things.
Number one, for making India stand tall again after the scourge of scams and scandals, which sadly marred another great Prime Minister's term, Dr. Manmohan Singh.
Second, he'll be remembered for placing India at the global high table of diplomacy.
By carving an identity of our own, whether it is actions against an irritating neighbour or whether it is staying away from conflicts and still getting our sovereign due.
Third, he'll be remembered for actually uniting India across the investment plane.
Fourth, he'll be remembered for galvanizing, as you rightly said, a political party and make it into a mean election machine, ably assisted, I would say, by Amit Shah.
But the point is that Narendra Modi is the brand.
He is the Mukota.
He is, as it were, the Amul girl.
He's the one who sells the brand, not in a negative way, not in a bad way.
But the dangers of that are equally strong.
What if something happens to Modi?
And let's imagine nothing happens.
Even then, he has to face the brunt of everything that is wrong and everything that is right.
So that is a precarious position, but he's managed it well.
Look, I've always said, you may have differences with Narendra Modi's ideology, but you can't differ from the fact that he is a third time elected prime minister of India.
not nominated, not sneaking in through the back door, nothing.
See, Nehru was more of a fate accompli.
Nehru was placed there by Mahatma Gandhi.
But in Narendra Modi's case, it's been a struggle.
Remember what happened post-Godhra?
There were tons of articles written, you know, he's done this, he's done that.
The Supreme Court exonerated him.
And it was that time that the Supreme Court exonerated him and the Congress was in part at the center.
So I have to say that he has stood the test of time, both as an administrator and as a leader.
You should see his personal popularity and you know this better than I do.
So in every which way, Narendra Modi ticks every brand box.
Brands are about relevance, brands are about benefits and brands are about stickiness.
Absolutely.
Sir, you know, Mr Vajpayee could not win the 2004 election, you know, after a very successful term, I would say, the Shining India campaign.
Then people saw Mr Manmohan Singh coming to power and repeating power in 2009.
So comparisons were made that Mr Manmohan Singh would repeat his government and be the PM for 10 years.

As you correctly say Mr. Modi has now been PM for three terms and you know after 2014's big success which many would say anti-incumbency against the UPA, corruption, scams maybe Mr. Modi got the benefit of that but 2019 was an even bigger victory between big state wins Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and many of these states won repeatedly by the BJP.
I am told by, you know, when I travel for elections, some leaders tell me that, you know, if an election is tight in the constituency, it seems right.
If they get a Modi rally, the election is sure to be won because he will swing at least, you know, at least 10% of the votes on that seat.
So that, I think, is also the popularity of the man.
And the popularity, do you think it's diminished in the last 12 years?
Do you think the brand is still very much intact?
The BJP may have taken a hit, but I don't think Mr. Modi's image has taken a hit.
Absolutely.
The brand is totally intact.
I'm so glad you asked this question.
On July 21, 2026, including on the CNN network, on Network 18 and other channels, I was asked, do you think the brand has taken a beating?
Has Modi been diminished?
No.
Remember, a great brand always scores corrects.
Remember what happened with Coca-Cola when they tried to tinker with the formula and tinker with the bottle and the packaging?
They came back.
When benzene traces were found in Perrier, the brand bounced back.
In our country, we saw the pesticide issue with Coca-Cola.
We saw the insecticide issue with Cadbury's.
The brands bounced back.
Because if the brand is intrinsically honest to its purpose, and has maintained a relationship which is non-transactional,
the brand will always work well.
A, B, in our country, we always believe that if a man has a family, then he will be corrupt.
The fact that he has no family and he then extrapolates it to say that 1.4 billion people are my family makes him even more endearing.
Yes, there are issues.
There are issues related to the minorities.
There are issues related to Hindus and Muslims, which I believe
he should steer clear from.
But that's part of the political conundrum that they face.
I genuinely believe, and I want to give you this example, and I've written about it.
I've known the prime minister since 1999.
And I've always been fond of him.
And I hope he's fond of me.
In 2008, I went to Gandhi Nagar, to his home.
And we were sitting down and chatting.
And he pulled out a book.
It was called Gift City.
So I said, yeh kya hai?
He says, we will replicate Singapore, Hong Kong, in Gujarat, in Ahmedabad.
I forgot about it.
I carried that coffee table book.
Fine.
When I was leaving, he said, toh Sohail bhai, Ratan Tata, nahi aap kal kahan ja rahe hain?
I said, mai Bombay ja rahe hain.
Will you be meeting Radhan Tata?
I said, yes.
He's saying, tell Radhan Tata to bring the Nano to Gujarat.
He's saying, remember when the Parsis came to India, they came to Nausari.
So he says, and tell them that it's time to return.
I went and communicated ad verbatim to Mr. Tata.
To cut a long story short, the Nano came to Sanant.
And it transformed Gujarat as the Detroit for India.
Please remember the person who had done it before was Jayalalitha.
Today, Gujarat is a hub for the auto industry like no one can imagine.
It was Narendra Modi.
And it was his vision.
It was his insistence.
And I can tell you, Aman, that clearances were given within 48 hours.
It was on your network.
on CNN, IBM, on CNBC, that I did a conversation with Mr. Tata, and it's available on YouTube, blah, blah, blah.
Mr. Tata there said, he says, I will always admire and thank Narendra Modi because he gave Nano a home.
Now that is the respect that industry had for him.
So when a person is respected to this extent, I wrote a piece which the prime minister was gracious enough to tweet, where I talked about his 12 years as prime minister.
And I began with Nehru.
I said, at Nehru's time, he was forced to do a couple of things.
The state had to invest in bulwark sectors.
But Narendra Modi didn't have to, but he did.
He set up more IIMs in five years than they were set up right through from independence till he took over.
Today, aims are all across the country.
IITs are across the country.
He's giving a push to RECs.
He's giving a push to MSMEs.
Now, this happens when a prime minister leads from the front.
when the Prime Minister's office, whether it's PK Mishra or Shaktikanth Das, are brilliant bureaucrats.
They know that they have to deliver.
They are not the bureaucrats who will have a problem for every solution.
So, a great leader also surrounds himself with good people.
And that is his brilliant hallmark.

The 2024 election, you know, BJP coming down to 240, lot was made of it that Mr. Modi is losing a bit of his luster and, you know, but after that, we saw how, as you correctly say, course corrected, these big wins first in Haryana, the state we, you live in, then in, you know, Maharashtra, Bengal right now, West Bengal, nobody gave BJP that chance that BJP can win so big.
All these states, Delhi, you know, Kejriwal going out of power after almost a decade, but these are big state election wins after that 240 setback.
What do you think Modi did different after that 2024, a bit of a setback, to course correct and bring around this big state election?
So, you have to understand his thinking process.
Modi recognizes failure, but he also knows that failure is only in the interim.
And that failure must demand some level of course correction.
So, what did he do?
Let's go step by step.
In Bengal, he set up the state machinery like never before.
I'm from Calcutta.
I was born and raised there.
I can tell you, Aman, that you will see a new Bengal in the next four years.
The investments have already begun to flow in.
I have seen Bengal from 1963 when I was born.
In 65, you had the UDF government.
Then you had Siddharth Shankar Ray.
Then you had Jyoti Basu.
You had Buddhadev Bhattacharya.
You had Mamata Banerjee.
Ruined the state.
They ruined the state because of petty politics.
Industry fled.
Young people fled.
Today, more Bengalis are outside Bengal and deeply successful than they are inside Bengal.
That will change.
Haryana, although I genuinely feel that the Prime Minister must take notice of the fact that Gurugram is under constant pressure.
Now, you know, people might say that, oh, Congress did it, but, you know, they've been in power for three terms, so there is course correction needed here, as will happen in Delhi.
See, Modi is a very, very tough taskmaster.
All those who think that Modi is forgiving of bad performances, no.
Modi is only interested in perform or perish.
And you will see that happen.
That's why you had the state elections in a different milieu.
The RSS, which was not involved in the UP Lok Sabha elections, is now fully back.
So Modi understands the power of allies.
You remember, it was the same Chandra Babu Naidu who didn't have very nice things to say about the Prime Minister.
Today?
The biggest thing about great leadership and great brands is the absence of an ego.
Now, can you imagine if Narendra Modi had said, Chandrababu Naidu had said this about me, then why should I befriend him?
People are mistaken that the alliance was only for power.
Of course it was for power.
But the alliance is much deeper.
Modi also respects people who have helped him.
Modi is a great friend of friends.
In the sense, people who have worked through the party.
I don't know if you remember, he was doing an election rally in Bengal.
And then he came back when the results were declared and when the swearing in happened of Shivendu Adhikari.
There was the oldest Bengali gentleman who was a colleague, if I remember right, of Deen Dayal Upadhyay Ji.
He was on stage and he was felicitated by Narendra Modi.
Modi didn't have to do it.
Now a lot of stupid people would say, oh he did it for the optics, even if he did it for the optics.
Ahankar is the worst thing that a great leader can have.
Entitlement is the worst thing that a great leader can have.
And my problem is, and I have all the respect for the Gandhis, blah, blah, blah, but the difference is the BJP is a political party.
The Congress is still an HUF lala company.
So, when we speak of the challenge to Narendra Modi, obviously, there will be a political challenge.
The Congress party has been in power for very long before him.
Right now, the Congress seems to be fancing its chances for 2029.
We have Mr. Rahul Gandhi in this new avatar.
I would say a Gen Z avatar, you know, reaching out to the youth.
This whole CJP protest has happened which Congress has tried to piggyback on and to get the youth on its side.
Do you think Rahul Gandhi has it in him to challenge or maybe defeat somebody like Narendra Modi in 2029 or do you think it's a far short story?
It's a great question, Aman, but go back into Indian history.
Other than Nehru, India has never predicted a future Prime Minister.
Let's take a pause.
When Pandit Nehru died on May 27, 1964, the interim Prime Minister was Gulzari Lananda.
Then you had Lal Bahadur Shastri.
No one thought.
When Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji passed away in Takshent, we all thought, you know, it'd be Moraji Desai.
But again, Gulzari Lal Nanda, interim, Indira Gandhi.
After Indira Gandhi, Mrs. Gandhi, when she demoted office in 1977, we had Moraji Desai, right up to 1980.
You had Mrs. Gandhi back.
After that you had Chandrasekhar, Deva Gowda, Vajpayee in two governments before his 1999 government.
You had I.K.
Gujral.
You had Narasimha Rao from 1991.
Narasimha Rao had packed his bags to move back to Hyderabad.
So, India has never predicted a future Prime Minister.

Even in 2013, when the announcement was made by Rajnath Singh that we have decided that Narendra Modi will be our Prime Ministerial campaign, a lot of people were thinking that Lal Krishna Advani would be the... Prime Minister.
...candidate.
It didn't happen.
So, you can't predict what will happen.
A. B. Rahul Gandhi, and I like what you said, Rahul Gandhi has used the position of the leader of opposition as a position of disruption.
Brands that want to take on other brands are always disruptive by nature.
Either they're disruptive through value or disruptive in price.
I'm talking about FMCG brands.
My only issue with Rahul Gandhi is, and you know, I will never say he's anti-national, he's this, he's that, everyone's entitled to their opinion.
My issue with Rahul Gandhi is two, A, a lack of consistency.
B. He's not a great people, person, qua his party.
And you have seen that in the departures, where there was Himanta Biswa Sarma, where there was Jyotira Aditya Sindhya, where there was Jiten Prasad, Milind Deora.
These were his friends.
So I have a rule.
If you can't keep your friends together, how will you keep and attract strangers and make them your friends?
So there's a serious people issue, which I'm sure he will resolve.
So I will not say, will he become, will he not become?
Remember one thing.
Today, the BJP can be deemed the grand old party, but the Congress is the grand old party.
So you can never say never in politics.
How do you see the difference in the political outlook of, say, Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi?
How do they see the electorate as such?
So, Narendra Modi sees India and Indian-ness.
Rahul Gandhi, to my mind, sees communities and strata and caste.
Fine.
But the India today has changed.
You see, I've always said, you have to give credit where credit is due.
Rajiv Gandhi was the man who brought in technology, brought in computerization, brought in C dot with Sam Petroda.
But today's voter, first time voter who's 18 years old, doesn't remember Indira Gandhi.
He certainly doesn't remember Mrs. Gandhi.
He doesn't even remember Rajiv Gandhi.
So their context has changed.
If the Prime Minister has been Prime Minister for 12 years and someone turns 18, that means he was 6 when Modi took over.
So, can you imagine the context?
So, the context for the present day mid-voter base will be Dr. Manmohan Singh and Narendra Modi.
It will not even be Vajpayeeji.
So, in that context, it is very difficult for Rahul Gandhi to lean on lineage.
He must therefore lean on something more concrete.
The problem is that even though he may have the best intentions, which I'm sure he does, the machinery is absent.
And you tell me, Amar, the Congress came into existence thanks to A.O.
Hume.
They've been in existence for over a century.
Why could they not set up the machinery that Narendra Modi and the BJP has set up in the last 25 years?
It takes courage, it takes planning, but most importantly it takes process.
Modi is about process and passion.
Raoul Gandhi is about passion.
He has to invest in process.
My last question to you, Mr. Modi is now 75 plus, you know, sometimes we feel that he is the one pushing this BJP machinery alone.
You know, even in this Gen Z protest, finally Mr. Modi had to come out and put out that Instagram reel and, you know, put people at ease that, you know, I'm listening to you.
I forgive people who are abusing me.
Do you think BJP has any succession plan?
Is there a plan?
I'm sure.
I'm sure.
See,
The beauty about all political succession is the day you announce your successor, you're dead.
So A, you don't announce your successor because it can also lead to a fracturing of the party.
You know, once Kamal Nath very rightly said, when I asked him, I said, what is the issue?
He says the Gandhis are decent and the Gandhis are the glue for the Congress.
Today, Modi and Amit Shah are the glue for the party.
What will happen after Mr. Modi?
We don't know.
But the thing, Aman, to see is the party has been created.
It is much like I said on your channel again, on CNBC, about the House of Tata.
The House of Tata is above individuals.
It's about its alignment and association with trust.
So individuals can come and go.
The House of Tata will remain.
In a similar vein, the BJP will always be a strong party.
And it is driven by party ideology.
It is driven by seva bhao.
It is guided, for whatever reason, ideological or otherwise by the RSS.
So it's deep rooted.
It's not tukka bazi.
It's not fly by night.
You know, they have an ideology which allows them to work within a principled ecosystem.
You may disagree with the ecosystem, but the ecosystem exists.
Well, absolutely.
And that's what Mr. Swael said very clearly, saying that it is the brand Modi, which has still not diminished or lacked, you know, lots of cluster.
even after being 25 years in power.

And during this 25 years, especially the 12 years he's been in Delhi, he's also built a BJP machinery, a background, I would say the background machinery is now so strong that it also is elevating the brand Modi when it comes to the big elections.
Thank you so much, Mr. Suhail Seth, for joining us on CNN News 18.
Thank you so much.
